text: Letters that we write in a message in the email message, okay. So we send a packet from a transmitter to a receiver. So we can think of it in our daily life as an email message, and we let this packet get a header in front. That means like when we write an email, we said we are going to add our address and of course the address of the destination, right? So that kind of information is the header of the email message that we write. And the same holds here. We have the base the information that is included in the payload, and then we have the header that carries the so called control information. Examples are the sender's address and the destination's address. Now in this header there may be other control information on top of the transmitters and receivers' address. Now in any RQ techniques, what we do is given a transmitter and a receiver, and given a packet.
